chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The example of the hypocrite is like the example of the trunk of a palm tree. Its owner intended to benefit from it in one of his constructions, but it did not stand straight for him in the place he intended. So he moved it to another place, but it did not stand straight for him. So the end of that was that he burned it with fire.'

key_terms.جِذْعِ النَّخْلِ: The trunk/stump of a palm tree

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphorical example of a hypocrite given in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the internal structural defect of the hypocrite through the metaphor of a palm trunk that, despite attempts to repurpose it for construction, remains unstable and ultimately is consumed by fire. This imagery underscores the Shia scholarly view that hypocrisy is not merely outward deception but a fundamental incompatibility with truth, rendering the individual useless in both this world and the Hereafter. The 'fire' signifies the inevitable consequence of this inherent misalignment with divine reality.
